items.title: Mahedi follows six-for with ton as NCL turns into run-fest
items.summary: Shak Mahedi was the standout performer, following up his six-wicket haul on the opening day with a commanding century to put Khulna in a strong position against Rajshahi at Mirpur’s Sher-e-Bangla National Cricket Stadium.

items.title: Mushfiqur, Shanto give Bangladesh big lead after Mahmud, Ebadot dismantle Afghanistan
items.summary: Bangladesh ended the third day of the one-off Test in Abu Dhabi 329 runs ahead with four second-innings wickets in hand

items.title: BCB investigates Nahid Rana’s back pain
items.summary: Doubts are growing over Bangladesh pacer Nahid Rana’s participation in the upcoming West Indies Test series, although the Bangladesh Cricket Board (BCB) is yet to rule him out.

items.title: Mostary: I am so happy about my century
items.summary: She made 118 off 134 against Australia in Brisbane, the highest score by a Bangladesh batter in ODIs

items.title: Voll’s blitz overshadows Mostary’s record ton as Australia seal series
items.summary: Bangladesh had posted their highest ODI total against Australia, finishing on 220 for six, but the hosts made light work of the target, reaching 222 for one in just 28.1 overs with 131 balls to spare.

items.title: Shanto, Mushfiqur miss tons but put Tigers in command
items.summary: Skipper Najmul Hossain Shanto and veteran Mushfiqur Rahim fell short of centuries but combined for a 159-run stand to push Bangladesh’s lead past 300 on Day 3 of the one-off Test against Afghanistan in Abu Dhabi on Sunday.

items.title: Rahmat, Malik fifties lead Afghanistan's strong reply
items.summary: Afghanistan managed to chip away at Bangladesh's 346 all-out and were only 135 away by stumps on the second day

items.title: Aliss Al Islam in Litton-led Bangladesh squad for ODI tri-series
items.summary: The mystery spinner is uncapped in ODI cricket, but has played one T20I so far

items.title: Afghanistan fast bowlers hit back after Bangladesh's strong start
items.summary: For Bangladesh, Shadman Islam, Tanzid Hasan and Litton Das made fifties

items.title: Sutherland and Litchfield lead Australia to quick and convincing win in ODI series opener
items.summary: Bangladesh were bowled out for 166 with only Ritu Moni showing any intent with the bat, and it took Australia just 25.4 overs to finish off the chase

items.title: Bangladesh opt to bat and pick Nayeem Hasan
items.summary: Bangladesh opted for Ebadot Hossain in place of Shoriful Islam while Afghanistan went for a batting-heavy line-up

items.title: Sultana: Bangladesh 'can surprise any team when we perform as a whole unit'
items.summary: The Bangladesh captain and coach David Hemp emphasised a positive mindset ahead of their first ever ODI in Australia

items.title: Stand-in captain McGrath has 'absolutely no idea' about her batting position
items.summary: "We have to be very positive... and we will definitely play our A-game against them," Bangladesh captain Nigar Sultana says ahead of the first ODI

items.title: Afghanistan look to tick boxes in rare Test outing against confident Bangladesh
items.summary: The win in Darwin is still fresh in the memory but Bangladesh have more than one form concern, while Afghanistan will hope to start afresh under new captain Rahmat Shah
